section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes the findings of a single study that investigated the hypothesis that higher self-compassion among college women, both relative to others and personal mean levels, would be protective against interactions with body-focused others. The results supported this, showing that self-compassion buffered negative relationships between body-focused interactions and body appreciation, intuitive eating, and negative affect. The study also highlighted the temporal variability of self-compassion and body-focused interactions.
